51288050.protein: Tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 11
51288050.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human RANKL by surface plasmon resonance analysis
51288050.references_previous: Reference 37: Zhang, S.; Liu, C.; Huang, P.; Zhou, S.; Ren, J.; Kitamura, Y.; Tang, P.; Bi, Z.; Gao, B. The affinity of human RANK binding to its ligand RANKL. Arch. Biochem. Biophys. 2009, 487, 49–53.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface Plasmon: Surface Plasmon Resonance. Studies were performed using a BIACore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare). Approximately 9000 response units (RU) of hRANKL, 300 RU of hRANKL, or 17 000 RU of hTNF were covalently immobilized onto sensor chip by a standard amine-coupling procedure. In binding assay, compounds were injected in a dilution series using 10 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, and 0.005% (v/v) Tween-20 as running buffer. DMSO in running buffer [1% (v/v)] was used as a detergent control. Kd determination experiments were performed using single-cycle kinetics with 30 s contact time and 30 μL/min flow rate at 20 °C. Kd values were calculated using steady state analysis at equilibrium with BIACore T200 evaluation software version 1.0 (GE Healthcare). In competition assay, compounds were incubated with indicated concentrations of hRANKL for 1 h and then injected to the chip. Data were corrected by subtraction of detergent control.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption - I binding to RANKL: Compound 1 binding to RANKL was analyzed with SPR, and the dissociation constant (Kd = 9.8 μM) was calculated. (I) In a competition assay, 1 at indicated concentrations remarkably inhibited RANKL binding to its receptor RANK.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption - I inhibiting RANKL-RA: Compound 1 at indicated concentrations remarkably inhibited RANKL binding to its receptor RANK.
original_paragraph.Table 5 - SPR Binding Assays of Indole D: compounds binding affinity (Kd) 2 2.7 μM 7 3.1 μM 29 3.5 μM 34 614 nM
original_paragraph.Results Section - Analysis of the Bindin: According to SPR analysis, 1 has higher binding affinity for RANKL (Kd = 9.8 μM) than OP3-4 and L3-3 (Kd = 284.4 and 17.3 μM, respectively). The binding affinity of RANKL for RANK was reported as 0.11 nM.37 We retested this value (0.1 nM, Figure S2, Supporting Information), and compound 1 inhibited RANKL binding to its receptor RANK in a dose-dependent manner with IC50 = 26.2 μM. The equilibrium binding curve fits are shown in Figure 2H and 2I. This result indicated the direct binding of 1 for RANKL and that 1 has the property of impeding RANKL/RANK protein interaction.
original_paragraph.Results Section - Inhibition of RANKL-In: The binding activity to RANKL of compounds 2, 7, 29, and 34 was also determined by SPR binding assays, and they displayed much higher affinity for RANKL with Kd values of 2.7 μM, 3.1 μM, 3.5 μM, and 614 nM, respectively (Table 5). Interestingly, 34 displayed weak affinity for TNF (93.6 μM, Figure S4, Supporting Information). As to its highest affinity to RANKL, 34 was chosen as a prototype for further examination in our subsequent studies.

It is well known that bone resorption is a characteristic feature of osteoclasts during bone remodeling. RANKL/RANK interaction could induce the bone resorption activity of mature osteoclasts; thus, we evaluated the effect of 34 on RANKL-induced bone resorption subsequently. As shown in Figure 5A, almost no resorption was detected in bone slices treated with 5 μM 34 while obvious resorbing pits were formed in the RANKL-treated group as visualized by toluidine blue staining. 34 (1, 2.5 μM) also significantly decreased the percentage of resorbed area. Besides, the calculated bone resorption shown in Figure 5B was consistent with Figure 5A.
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Effect of compound 34 on bone resorption of osteoclasts. (A) Mature osteoclasts were seeded onto bovine femur bone slices in 96-well plates. Next day, cells were induced with 30 ng/mL M-CSF and 50 ng/mL RANKL combined with the indicated concentrations of 34 for 2 days. Bone slices were sonicated to remove extraneous cells. Slices were fixed with 2.5% glutaraldehyde. Slices were imaged using a Zeiss LSM 800 confocal microscope with 100× magnification. (B) Pit areas were quantified using ImageJ software and presented graphically. Pit area in control was set as 1; data was expressed as fold change relative to the control: (***P < 0.001 vs control
original_paragraph.Figure 6 caption: Effect of compound 34 on osteoclast-specific genes expression and c-Fos/NFATc1-signaling pathway in vitro. (A–C) BMMs were stimulated with M-CSF and RANKL in the presence of different doses of 34 for 3 days. Osteoclasts marker gene levels of (A) TRAP, (B) NFATc1, and (C) cathepsin K were determined by quantitative RT-PCR analysis in BMMs at indicated concentrations of 34 in combination with M-CSF and RANKL. Results were normalized to β-actin expression and expressed as fold change relative to gene expression in control cells: (**) P < 0.01 and (***) P < 0.001 vs control. (D) 34 in increasing doses were incubated with BMMs for 3 days in combination with 30 ng/mL M-CSF and 50 ng/mL RANKL. Then expression of NFATc1 and c-fos was examined by WB. Actin acted as the internal control.

data_analysis.reference_description: Detergent control (1% DMSO in running buffer)
data_analysis.software: Biacore T200 evaluation software version 1.0 (GE Healthcare)

51288062.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human RANKL by surface plasmon resonance analysis
51288062.references_previous: Reference 37: Zhang, S.; Liu, C.; Huang, P.; Zhou, S.; Ren, J.; Kitamura, Y.; Tang, P.; Bi, Z.; Gao, B. The affinity of human RANK binding to its ligand RANKL. Arch. Biochem. Biophys. 2009, 487, 49–53.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface Plasmon: Surface Plasmon Resonance. Studies were performed using a BIACore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare). Approximately 9000 response units (RU) of hRANKL, 300 RU of hRANKL, or 17 000 RU of hTNF were covalently immobilized onto sensor chip by a standard amine-coupling procedure. In binding assay, compounds were injected in a dilution series using 10 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, and 0.005% (v/v) Tween-20 as running buffer. DMSO in running buffer [1% (v/v)] was used as a detergent control. Kd determination experiments were performed using single-cycle kinetics with 30 s contact time and 30 μL/min flow rate at 20 °C. Kd values were calculated using steady state analysis at equilibrium with BIACore T200 evaluation software version 1.0 (GE Healthcare). In competition assay, compounds were incubated with indicated concentrations of hRANKL for 1 h and then injected to the chip. Data were corrected by subtraction of detergent control.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption - I binding to RANKL: Compound 1 binding to RANKL was analyzed with SPR, and the dissociation constant (Kd = 9.8 μM) was calculated. (I) In a competition assay, 1 at indicated concentrations remarkably inhibited RANKL binding to its receptor RANK.

original_paragraph.Results Section - Analysis of the Bindin: According to SPR analysis, 1 has higher binding affinity for RANKL (Kd = 9.8 μM) than OP3-4 and L3-3 (Kd = 284.4 and 17.3 μM, respectively). The binding affinity of RANKL for RANK was reported as 0.11 nM.37 We retested this value (0.1 nM, Figure S2, Supporting Information), and compound 1 inhibited RANKL binding to its receptor RANK in a dose-dependent manner with IC50 = 26.2 μM. The equilibrium binding curve fits are shown in Figure 2H and 2I. This result indicated the direct binding of 1 for RANKL and that 1 has the property of impeding RANKL/RANK protein interaction.
original_paragraph.Results Section - Inhibition of RANKL-In: The binding activity to RANKL of compounds 2, 7, 29, and 34 was also determined by SPR binding assays, and they displayed much higher affinity for RANKL with Kd values of 2.7 μM, 3.1 μM, 3.5 μM, and 614 nM, respectively (Table 5). Interestingly, 34 displayed weak affinity for TNF (93.6 μM, Figure S4, Supporting Information). As to its highest affinity to RANKL, 34 was chosen as a prototype for further examination in our subsequent studies.

It is well known that bone resorption is a characteristic feature of osteoclasts during bone remodeling. RANKL/RANK interaction could induce the bone resorption activity of mature osteoclasts; thus, we evaluated the effect of 34 on RANKL-induced bone resorption subsequently. As shown in Figure 5A, almost no resorption was detected in bone slices treated with 5 μM 34 while obvious resorbing pits were formed in the RANKL-treated group as visualized by toluidine blue staining. 34 (1, 2.5 μM) also significantly decreased the percentage of resorbed area. Besides, the calculated bone resorption shown in Figure 5B was consistent with Figure 5A.
